title: Row-Level Security (RLS) & Multi-Tenancy
description: Isolate tenant data at the database engine level using CREATE POLICY, current_setting(), and Row-Level Security.

data.text: **Row-Level Security (RLS)** restricts which rows are returned or modified based on the user executing the query. Even if an application query forgets a `WHERE tenant_id = $1` clause, PostgreSQL enforces the security policy at the storage layer, preventing cross-tenant data leaks.
Multi-Tenant RLS Implementation with Session Settings

data.title: Enabling RLS on Documents Table
data.content: Policy reads app.current_tenant_id from session configuration.

data.text: Row-Level Security at the Tenant Boundary

RLS applies a policy to every query automatically, so an application cannot forget a `WHERE tenant_id = ...` clause and leak another tenant's rows. The policy reads the current tenant from a session setting that the application sets at the start of each request. Table owners and superusers bypass RLS unless `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is set.

data.title: A tenant-isolation policy
data.content: The application sets `app.tenant_id` per request; the policy compares it to the row's tenant. FORCE makes the policy apply even to the table owner.

data.title: RLS is defeated by a missing setting or an owner connection
data.text: If the application forgets to set `app.tenant_id`, `current_setting(..., true)` returns NULL and the policy compares against NULL, which matches nothing — a fail-closed default if you use the two-argument form, but a fail-open mistake if your policy is written to allow NULL. Creating the table as the application role makes it the owner, and owners bypass RLS; use `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` or a dedicated owner role. Test RLS with the exact role and connection settings the application uses.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RLS transparently filters rows for non-superusers based on defined policies.
Combine `current_setting('app.tenant_id')` with RLS for multi-tenant SaaS.
Table owners and superusers bypass RLS by default unless `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is set.
